exact_facts.label: L10
exact_facts.text: [L10] For clause (a) only, under its stated choice assumptions, an AC coordinate function is the integral of its integrable derivative; the derivative of a bounded nondecreasing function on a compact interval is integrable with integral bounded by its total increase. The indefinite integral of an L1 function is AC ([[thm-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus-for-absolutely-continuous-functions]], [[thm-the-derivative-of-an-increasing-function-is-measurable-integrable-and-bounded-by-its-total-increase]], [[cor-the-indefinite-integral-of-an-l-one-function-is-absolutely-continuous]]).

exact_current_proof_steps.claim: (Endpoint absolute continuity and extension.) Let $\gamma$ and $x$ be as in (a). By [L9] choose a Lorentz-orthonormal basis $e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ at $x$, with $e_0$ future-directed. An invertible linear change of any chart centred at $x$ gives coordinates $z$ whose coordinate basis at $x$ is this basis, hence $g_{ab}(x)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. After shrinking to a coordinate ball there is $C<\infty$ such that $|v|_{\mathrm e}\le C v^0$ for every nonzero future causal vector based in that ball. To prove this, otherwise there are base points $q_n\to x$ and coordinate unit future causal vectors $v_n$ with $v_n^0<1/2$. Pass to a convergent subsequence of the unit vectors. Its unit limit $v$ satisfies $g_x(v,v)\le0$ and $g_x(v,N_x)\le0$; the latter is strict by [L9], so $v$ is future causal. Thus $v^0>0$ and $|v_s|\le v^0$ in the chosen orthonormal basis, giving $v^0\ge1/\sqrt2$, a contradiction. The coordinate $z^0$ is therefore strictly increasing on future causal curves in this ball, and supplies the local strict temporal coordinate. Choose $a<b$ so the tail of $\gamma$ stays in this chart, write $y=z\circ\gamma$, and extend $y(b)=z(x)$. Put $\tau=y^0$; on each compact subinterval of $[a,b)$, the AC chain rule and FTC give $\tau'>0$ and $|y'|_{\mathrm e}\le C\tau'$ almost everywhere and make $\tau$ strictly increasing. Its continuous endpoint extension is bounded and nondecreasing on $[a,b]$, so [L10] gives $\tau'\in L^1[a,b]$. Consequently each component of $y'$ is integrable on $[a,b]$. For $t<b$ the local FTC gives $y(t)=y(a)+\int_a^t y'$ componentwise; letting $t\uparrow b$ gives the same identity at $b$, since the integral of an L1 function is continuous and $y(t)\to y(b)$. Thus the endpoint extension of $y$ is AC on $[a,b]$ by [L10], and retains its original nonzero future causal velocity almost everywhere. Choose a future timelike $w\in T_xM$; [L4] supplies a short geodesic $\beta(s)=\exp_x(sw)$ with $\beta(0)=x$, whose tangents are future timelike by [L3]. Concatenate the now AC closed tail with $\beta$ by [L7] and leave the earlier part of $\gamma$ unchanged. This defines the required future causal $\tilde\gamma$ on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ and proves (a). The past case reverses time.
